jobs.description:
Bojon Logistics is looking for a motivated Key Account Manager to help us grow and take care of our new clients.

You will help build strong customer relationships, onboard new accounts, identify business opportunities and ensure a high level of service.

✅ 35-hour work week
✅ Hybrid working arrangement
✅ Commercial and customer-focused role
✅ Opportunity to learn and grow with the company

📍 Copenhagen area
📩 Send us your CV and a short introduction.

Head of Engineering to join a technology-driven intelligence company serving the renewable energy industry

Please note: We do not offer relocation or sponsorship for this position, and only candidates able to work on location will be considered

Want to lead a small team of developers and data scientists while staying close to the code? Want real ownership of an established platform inside a growing 20-person startup? Want to enable a greener future by helping major energy companies decide where to invest in renewable energy?

Then this might be your next role

Join Aegir Insights and get a unique opportunity to join a workplace where you can make a difference every day, whilst being part of a young, agile and fast-paced company.

We are accelerating the transition towards renewable energy sources worldwide by providing products that enable developers, investors, consultancies, suppliers, and governments across onshore wind, offshore wind, solar, storage and data centers to make smarter decisions, faster.

As Head of Engineering, you will own the platform behind our products and build the engineering team that runs it.

The platform combines curated data on more than 100,000 renewable energy projects, geospatial analytics, and financial models

Built on a stack of

React/TypeScript, Python/FastAPI, MongoDB, AWS, and Kubernetes.

The role spans technical direction, hands-on engineering, team building, delivery, and building the engineering function in Copenhagen

You will come in at a critical time in our growth and take the lead of a small team of 5 technical profiles ranging from Software developers to data scientists

You report to the founders and work closely with our commercial team and our in-house renewable energy experts.

This is not a management-only role. It is a hands-on engineering leadership role for someone equally comfortable designing and implementing a Python service, reviewing a data model, debugging a production issue, hiring a senior engineer, and explaining an architecture decision to the board.

Your key tasks will be to

• Own the technical direction of the platform: architecture, data foundations, security, reliability and build-versus-buy decisions

• Remain hands-on: design, build and review production code, particularly across our Python/FastAPI backend, APIs, data services and platform infrastructure

• Own systems end-to-end: be willing to trace a problem from React/TypeScript through APIs and data models to MongoDB, AWS/Kubernetes and external services, and fix it at the appropriate layer

• Build the Copenhagen engineering team: define the roles, hire as the business case develops, and set an operating model that gives strong engineers real ownership

• Translate product priorities set with the founders and commercial team into a technical roadmap and delivery plan

• Raise the engineering bar: establish pragmatic patterns for architecture, testing, APIs, code review, deployment, observability and documentation - and demonstrate those standards through your own engineering work

• Lay the foundation for secure multi-tenant SaaS, including authentication, authorization and permission-aware workflows

• Own the technical foundations for AI-native products and workflows, including our MCP infrastructure and secure programmatic access to Aegir's data, analytics and financial models

During the first 6–12 months, we expect the role to remain about 50-60% hands-on while you learn the platform, establish the technical direction, and make a plan for how to grow the department.

We imagine that you

• Have an educational background in computer science, software engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical engineering experience

• Bring experience from similar software engineering roles

• With experience in Python, APIs, data-intensive systems, and cloud architecture, while being comfortable working across a modern React/TypeScript stack

• Ideally with experience leading engineers or engineering teams, while remaining hands-on in recent roles

• Fluent english

Extra point if you have

• Have improved a live, complex platform without reaching for a ground-up rewrite

• Have personally designed, built and operated production backend systems and APIs, including data models, authentication/authorisation, asynchronous workloads and integrations between systems

• Have experience designing data-intensive applications, analytical systems or data pipelines, and making pragmatic decisions about performance, cost and maintainability

• Pragmatic and structured: you make trade-offs explicit and tie them to cost, risk and customer value

• A people leader who hires well and gives senior engineers real ownership without losing alignment with the business

• Clear, top-down communication with founders, commercial leaders and domain experts who are not software engineers

• Comfortable in a small company: you set direction, write code and get close enough to users and the work to help the team move

• Experience with geospatial systems, financial modelling or the energy sector is an advantage Comfortable using modern AI coding tools as part of everyday engineering and interested in how AI changes software development itself - not just in adding LLM features to products

Working at Aegir Insights

Joining Aegir Insights means joining an international and dedicated team that moves with strategic intent on new ideas and enjoys learning new things. We encourage innovative and lateral thinking to achieve our goals.

We offer a respectful, diverse, and international working environment (our company language is English).

We have high ambitions, and you will take part in our growth journey by actively helping shape our culture and technical direction.

We offer a competitive remuneration package:

• Salary according to experience

• Flexible working conditions (minimum 3 office days per week in Copenhagen office)

• Subsidized lunch when working from the office

• 10% pension contribution and company pension scheme

• Insurance scheme including private health insurance

We are located in the heart of Copenhagen at Havnegade 27 st, 1058 Copenhagen.

About Aegir Insights

Aegir Insights is a technology-driven company offering decision-making software, data and intelligence products for the renewable energy sector. We combine data science and deep industry experience to help developers, investors, suppliers and governments make decisions.

Would you like to help accelerate the world's transformation to renewable energy?

Then apply now

We encourage everyone to apply, regardless of their background. We will conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will close this job advertisement as soon as we have identified a successful candidate. If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Casper Høgh by e-mail at Csh@ing.dk or on  50 50 25 70

Covidence is a growing international technology company developing and manufacturing specialised,

miniaturised electronics used in demanding applications around the world. With subsidiaries in the UK and

Ireland, we work across borders and collaborate with colleagues and customers internationally.

We’re now looking for a curious and hands-on Marketing Student Assistant to join our commercial team in

Risskov. If you’re looking to turn what you learn in your studies into real-world experience, this is an opportunity to get involved, take responsibility and see your work make a difference in an international business.

Get hands-on marketing experience in a growing technology company

Want to see what marketing looks like beyond textbooks, lectures and theory?

At Covidence Group, you’ll get to work on real marketing materials that are used by our customers, sales team and partners. You’ll work closely with our commercial organisation and get an inside look at how marketing supports an international B2B technology business. It’s a varied role where you can combine content, design, digital marketing and practical project work — and where the work you do will be visible and have a real purpose.

What you’ll do

You’ll become part of the commercial team and help make sure our products, materials and marketing presence are always ready to go.

Your day-to-day work will include:

• Create visual content: Design banners, icons, presentations and other visual assets for digital and print use.

• Bring products to life: Keep product documentation, datasheets and other materials accurate, clear and up to date.

• Keep our digital presence fresh: Manage and update content on our customer portal.

• Make information easy to find: Maintain our digital and physical library of marketing and product materials.

• Get trade shows ready: Help prepare presentations, printed materials, product information and practical logistics for exhibitions and customer events.

• Take ownership of projects: Pick up smaller projects and special tasks as they arise, with the opportunity to shape how things are done.

This is a hands-on marketing role designed for someone who wants to learn by doing. You’ll get involved in the practical work behind B2B marketing — creating visual content, preparing marketing materials, supporting trade shows and helping turn ideas into something tangible. It’s a varied role where you’ll gain experience across different areas of marketing rather than focusing on just one.

You’re the right person if you

• Are studying marketing, communications, multimedia design, business, or a similar field

• Are looking for a role where you can put your knowledge into practice and gain hands-on experience

• Are organised, independent and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage different tasks and priorities

• Have strong, natural English writing skills and feel confident communicating in English

• Enjoy turning information into clear, useful and professional content

• Have experience with Adobe Creative Suite is a plus

• Have some experience with content creation or document management – this is an advantage, but not a requirement

Most importantly, you’re curious, willing to learn and happy to get stuck into a variety of tasks.

You will work primarily from our office in Risskov. As the role involves close collaboration with the commercial team and hands-on work with physical materials, being comfortable working on-site is important.

What we offer

• A paid, part-time student position in a growing international technology company

• Real responsibility from day one – your work will be used and have a visible impact

• The opportunity to build practical experience across content, design, digital marketing and B2B communications

• A varied role where you can learn, contribute and take ownership

• A small and collaborative team where you’ll work closely with colleagues across the business

• The opportunity to see how marketing connects with products, sales and customers in an international company

If you’re looking for a student job where you can create things, learn how a real business works and see the results of your work, we’d love to hear from you.

How to apply

Send a CV and a short note (3–4 paragraphs, not a generic cover letter) explaining why you are a good fit for this role. If you have a portfolio or other relevant examples of your work, you are also welcome to include or share it as part of your application.

Please submit your application through: www.covidence.com/job-openings

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to Mathias Borg on email: mbo@covidence.com.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  The application deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

Do you want to shape the future of analytics for the world's largest jewellery brand? Are you passionate about using data, insights, and technology to drive growth, influence strategy, and unlock commercial opportunities? Then you could be the Senior Manager, Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights we're looking for.

As Senior Manager, Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights, you will play a pivotal role in defining and driving Pandora's global eCommerce analytics agenda. This is a highly visible leadership position at the intersection of analytics, commercial strategy, and digital growth.

You will act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders across Global eCommerce, helping shape business decisions through data-driven insights and strategic recommendations. Leveraging a deep understanding of digital performance, customer behaviour, and commercial drivers, you will identify opportunities to accelerate growth, optimise performance, and strengthen Pandora's global eCommerce business.

Leading a team of analytics professionals, you will combine strategic thinking, business acumen, and analytical expertise to ensure data remains at the heart of decision-making across the organisation.

Key responsibilities

Commercial insights & business partnering

• 
Act as a trusted analytics partner to Global eCommerce leadership, shaping priorities and key business decisions.

• 
Identify growth opportunities across traffic, conversion, customer and product performance, and turn them into clear commercial recommendations.

• 
Lead deep dives into the key drivers of eCommerce performance and translate findings into actions that move the business.

Forecasting & performance management

• 
Own forecasting and performance measurement that support commercial planning and trading decisions.

• 
Define the KPIs and frameworks used to track and steer eCommerce growth.

• 
Continuously sharpen analytical approaches and decision-making tools.

Analytics strategy & Centre of Excellence

• 
Define the analytics strategy, priorities and roadmap for Global eCommerce.

• 
Lead Pandora's global eCommerce analytics community and set the standard for how analytics creates business value.

• 
Build analytical and commercial capability across the organisation through coaching and knowledge sharing.

eCommerce analytics platforms

• 
Act as business owner of Pandora's key eCommerce analytics platforms, ensuring they answer the questions that matter most to the business.

• 
Lead the Centre of Excellence around these platforms, connecting business needs with technology teams and vendor partners.

• 
Ensure stakeholders can rely on trusted, decision-ready data.

Team leadership

• 
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing analytics team.

• 
Build capabilities in analytics, storytelling, and stakeholder engagement.

• 
Foster a collaborative, curious and commercially minded culture.

What is needed to succeed

We imagine that you bring significant experience within eCommerce analytics, commercial analytics, digital analytics, business intelligence, or a related field, combined with a passion for translating data into business value and strategic impact.

Furthermore, we are looking for someone who has:

• 
Extensive experience working within eCommerce, digital, or commercial analytics environments.

• 
A strong track record of using analytics and insights to influence business strategy, trading performance, and commercial outcomes.

• 
Demonstrated success partnering with senior stakeholders and influencing decisions through data-driven recommendations.

• 
Strong business acumen and the ability to connect analytical findings to broader commercial objectives.

• 
Experience identifying growth opportunities and proactively defining analytical priorities and agendas.

• 
Experience leading and developing high-performing analytics teams.

• 
Strong knowledge of digital performance analytics, forecasting, experimentation, and performance measurement.

• 
Experience acting as business owner of web analytics platforms, ideally Adobe Analytics and Contentsquare or similar digital experience analytics tools.

• 
Experience setting the analytics agenda and ways of working within a global organisation.

• 
Experience working in complex, matrixed, international environments.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to structure ambiguous business questions into actionable analytical approaches.

• 
Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to engage and influence both technical and non-technical audiences.

• 
A continuous improvement mindset and passion for cultivating data-driven cultures.

We hope to see that you are:

• 
A commercially minded analytics leader who naturally connects data to business outcomes.

• 
A strategic thinker who can see the bigger picture while identifying the key drivers of performance.

• 
Comfortable moving between executive-level discussions and analytical deep dives.

• 
Curious, proactive, and confident challenging assumptions with data and insights.

• 
An inspiring people leader and coach.

• 
A strong communicator who can simplify complexity and translate analytics into actionable recommendations.

• 
Skilled at influencing stakeholders across all levels of the organisation.

• 
Collaborative and relationship-oriented.

• 
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity in a fast-paced international environment.

• 
Passionate about driving business performance through customer, commercial, and digital insights.

Your new team

You will join Pandora's Global eCommerce Analytics & Insights team, a critical function enabling data-driven growth across our global digital business.

Working closely with commercial, trading, marketing, product, technology, and analytics stakeholders, you will help shape the future of eCommerce analytics at Pandora and ensure insights play a central role in how we grow and evolve our digital business.

Additional information

• Global Career Band: 4A

Did we get your attention?

If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora's future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site: www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable, and inspirational, delivering a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting, and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion in 2025.

jobs.description:
Are you handy, motivated, and experienced with tires? 🔧 We are looking for several dedicated Tire Fitters for a client in the Brøndby area. Since this is a busy season, prior experience with tire fitting and balancing is required so you can hit the ground running!

💼 WHAT YOU GET

• Position: Full-time temporary position (Mid-September – End of December)
• Salary: DKK 173.60/hour + pension, holiday pay, and special savings (fritvalgskonto)
• Hours: Monday to Friday, 07:30 AM – 15:30 PM (overtime may occur)
• Workplace: A fast-paced, informal environment with great colleagues and a good sense of humor in Brøndby
📋 WHAT WE EXPECT

• Experience: You have proven experience with tire changing
• License: You hold a valid Category B driver's license
• Profile: You are responsible, independent, and in good physical shape (heavy lifting occurs)
• Language: You speak and understand English or Danish
🤝 WHY WORK WITH HUMANIZER?

• Flexibility: Opportunities tailored to fit your availability
• Benefits: A great way to earn extra money and gain hands-on experience
• Future: Many of our temporary positions open the door to permanent employment
🚀 APPLY TODAY!

Ready to join the team? Create your profile here: Humanizer.dk and mark it "tire fitter".

We look forward to hearing from you!

About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.

We require a physical presence in our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. We believe this enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles to build an impactful product that users love to use.

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

• 
Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

• 
OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

• 
Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

• 
Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

• 
Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

• 
Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

• 
Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

• 
Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

• 
Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

• 
Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

• 
Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

• 
Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

• 
Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

• 
Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

jobs.occupation: Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for byggeri og Bygni
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling

Research area and project description
Predictive control can reduce energy costs and CO2 emissions of heating and cooling homes. However, its performance depends on knowing when residents are home and what they find comfortable.

You will develop a natural-language interface, based on a large language model, between residents and a predictive controller. Residents can then tell the controller, when they are away, report how the rooms feel, or ask for a warmer bathroom etc. In return, the controller explains what it did and why, shows what the next hours cost in money and CO2, and suggests alternatives that residents can accept or decline. The comfort limits are thus set by the residents; with the information they need.

This dialogue can save energy in three ways. Knowing when people are home and which rooms they use enables occupancy-based control, heating only where and when needed. Reports on how the rooms feel train personal comfort models, so setpoints match each household. The third, and least explored, is energy sufficiency: residents knowingly accept less heating or cooling, for example 20 °C instead of 21.5 °C on an expensive evening, while remaining free to say no. A central question is whether explaining alternative control actions and their cost changes how residents judge the same indoor conditions (their thermal acceptability), and whether the change lasts. All three look the same on the energy meter, so the project must separate them.

Few people want a system that talks all the time. Residents differ in how much information they want, in what form, and whether the system should take the initiative or only respond when asked (proactive versus on-demand interaction). Engagement may also fade as the novelty wears off. The project will study these differences and design for them.

You will:
• couple the language model to the controller, so that residents' requests become control actions within safe limits
• run a climate chamber experiment on whether explanations change thermal acceptability
• carry out a field study in occupied Danish homes through a winter and a summer, covering heating and overheating
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a M.Sc. in engineering, computer science, building science or a related technical field. Applicants with a B.Sc. and at least one year of master's studies can apply through the 4+4 programme.

You should be able to program, preferably in Python, and be comfortable analysing data. Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: model predictive control or optimisation, large language models, statistics and the design of experiments with people, and field measurements in buildings. Nobody will have all of these, and you should be willing to learn what you lack.

The field study involves installing equipment in people's homes and talking with the residents, so you should be comfortable working with people. Danish is an advantage for the field work but not a requirement.

Applicants from neighbouring fields with relevant technical skills and a clear motivation for the topic are encouraged to apply.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Arhus C., Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
 
• Michael Dahl Knudsen, mdk@cae.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Massimo Fiorentini, massimo@cae.au.dk (co-supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:

Application deadline is 15 November 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 January 2027.
